accepted_interpretation.source_support: Writing the combined shift as delta, the proof inserts a Perron integral for the truncated sum over h, expands twice the real part of the Fourier transform into positive and negative phases, and rotates the two v-contours to opposite imaginary rays. Their sum gives a cosine-Gamma factor identified with the chi factor in the zeta functional equation. The expression becomes a Mellin contour involving zeta(1-s-delta); moving that contour left picks up poles at s=0 and s=-delta, exactly producing the target identity. A general Mellin-Fourier relation is also recorded for compactly supported functions on the positive reals.
